HYPOTHESIS (canonical, English): In the PCA on the 12 forms of capital (100-year bins, correlation-matrix PCA fitted on the full 4300–500 BCE series), both the Middle Neolithic (3400–3000 BCE) and the Younger Neolithic (2900–2300 BCE) occupy the low-capital-intensity end of PC1 (PC1 sign fixed positive toward overall capital intensity, corr(PC1, mean of 12 Z) = +0.557; PC1 explains 30.3% of variance). The Middle Neolithic (MN bins 3400–3000) is characterized by a DECLINING PC1 trend: from −0.58 (3400 BCE) to a trough of −1.78 (3000 BCE), mean −1.37, slope ≈ −0.26 PC1 units per century — i.e., the phase begins comparatively higher and steadily loses capital intensity. The Younger Neolithic (SG bins 2900–2300) is characterized by a FLUCTUATING, RECOVERING PC1: mean −1.12 (0.26 units above MN), ranging from −1.60 (2800 BCE) to −0.41 (2300 BCE), slope ≈ +0.12 units per century, with local recoveries at 2700 BCE (−0.68) and 2300 BCE (−0.41) — i.e., the phase starts low and progressively rebuilds capital intensity toward 2300 BCE. Phase drivers are asymmetric: within the Neolithic phases the PC1 score is depressed mainly by negative loadings of pottery form (ZKeform, loading −0.35, corr −0.67), axes/celts (ZBeil, −0.24), amber (Zamber, −0.24) and sickles (ZSichel, −0.15), whereas increases in PC1 are driven by copper/gold (ZCU_AU, +0.41, corr +0.78), pottery decoration (Zkeverz, +0.38), depots (ZHort, +0.34) and hatchets/swords (ZAxtSchwert, +0.30). Thus the two phases are best characterized not as a single uniform "low capital" stage but as two distinct trajectories: a Middle Neolithic erosion of capital intensity (especially declining house size and monument-related values within the phase) followed by a Younger Neolithic rebound led by metal, deposition and pottery-decoration practices, both phases remaining far below the later Bronze Age levels of PC1 (OBA/YBA reach +1.9 to +4.4). Secondary context: bin-level PC1 correlates strongly with landscape openness (pollen PC1 MEAN, r = 0.71 over 36 common bins), consistent with capital intensity tracking landn/openness over the full series; however, within the Middle Neolithic the coupling breaks down (openness rises sharply from −1.86 to +0.08 while PC1 falls), suggesting the MN decline is specific to capital practices rather than a purely environmental effect.

RESUMEN (ES): Ambas fases quedan en el extremo bajo de PC1 (intensidad de capital). El Neolítico Medio (media PC1 = −1.37) muestra una tendencia DECLINANTE (−0.58 en 3400 a.C. → −1.78 en 3000 a.C.; ≈ −0.26 unidades/siglo), mientras que el Neolítico Joven (media PC1 = −1.12, +0.26 por encima del MN) muestra una trayectoria FLUCTUANTE Y RECUPERADORA (−1.50 en 2900 → −0.41 en 2300 a.C.; ≈ +0.12 unidades/siglo, con máximos locales en 2700 y 2300 a.C.). Los drivers del aumento de PC1 son cobre/oro, decoración cerámica y depósitos; los que deprimen PC1 en estas fases son forma cerámica, hachas/celtas, ámbar y hoces. Correlación contextual PC1–apertura del paisaje (polen) = 0.71, aunque en el MN la apertura del paisaje sube mientras PC1 cae (desacoplamiento intrafase).

payload.workflow: 1) Loaded capital.csv (comma decimals): 39 rows x 15 cols, 100-year bins BCE 4300-500 (positive counting backward; verified identical to time_series_data.csv *_inter at CE=-BCE), 12 Z columns, no missing values, group labels MN=3400-3000 and SG=2900-2300 matching the question's phases. 2) Correlation-matrix PCA on the 12 re-standardized Z columns over the full 4300-500 BCE series via numpy SVD (sklearn unavailable). 3) PC1 sign convention: positive correlation with the mean of the 12 Z (corr = +0.557, no flip needed). 4) Extracted PC1 per 100-year bin (analysis/pc1_by_bin.csv) and loadings (analysis/pc1_loadings.csv). 5) Characterized MN (3400,3300,3200,3100,3000) and SG (2900..2300): means (-1.374 vs -1.117), ranges (1.199 vs 1.187), per-century trends (-0.259 vs +0.120), drivers via loadings. 6) Secondary context: pollen openness (Belau/Woserin MEAN, decimal=','), bin-level corr(PC1, MEAN) = 0.711 (n=36 bins), within-phase MN decoupling documented. Script: analysis/pca_capital_phases.py.
